issues.problem: Semantic merge break: the r2 test added in 3927e1a ('a pid file that cannot be written does not stop the grant') was written for H4b's old lock loop. Merging H4a 1799a7c replaced the loop (mkdir && write pid; ownerless check uses [[ ! -s lock/pid ]], which is true-ish for a directory), so the test now fails deterministically and the suite is red. CI test(claude)/test(codex) would fail.
issues.evidence: bash tests/run-all-tests.sh tests/hooks/test-user-consent.sh under SILVER_BULLET_RUNTIME=claude and codex: 'FAIL: a pid file that cannot be written does not stop the grant', 'FAIL: grant recorded without a pid file (expected granted, got unset)', 'FAIL: and the lock is released'; stderr: 'user-consent.sh: line 193: .../.consent.lock/pid: Is a directory' then 'sb-consent: another sb-consent is writing ...'. Same 3 failures in the coverage run.
issues.suggested_fix: Coordinate with H4a (owner of the lock code): either drop/rewrite this H4b test to H4a's semantics (an unwritable pid gives up with status 2 and leaves no lock), or have H4a treat a lock it just created as owned even if the pid write fails. Re-run test-user-consent.sh under both runtimes.

issues.problem: leanctx with only wire consent is enabled in Pi, and install-pi.py then adds 'npm:pi-lean-ctx' to ~/.pi/agent/settings.json packages, i.e. asks Pi to install an npm package without install consent. Now also reached from the graphify stack-optimizer pre:pi command.

issues.suggested_fix: Pass --enable-tool leanctx only when leanctx has both wire and install consent (or have install-pi.py take a separate --install-package flag).
